samples.summary: The case-insensitive `data:` fix in `imageInline` has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes `image.src.startsWith('data:')` to `/^data:/i.test(image.src)` and its own comment says "Spelled `DATA:` this test used to answer `false`, so a data URL was emitted inline with `inlineImages` off — the one thing this branch exists to prevent." I grepped `packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts` for `DATA:` / `inlineImages` (lines 343, 361, 385, 396, 577, 669): every data-URI case is spelled lowercase `data:image/png;base64,...`. Reverting the `/i` would leave the whole suite green while an uppercase-scheme data URL is again inlined with `inlineImages: false` (SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI is itself `/i`, so it passes the src gate).

The new helper's docstring makes `allowZero` the crux: "a page dimension of 0 is as broken as a negative one, while a margin of 0 is a legitimate edge-to-edge layout." The new `parsePageSetup` tests (packages/docs/test/import/docx-parser.test.ts:196-197) only cover non-numeric and negative margins, and the pgSz table covers zero only for page size. Grepping `pgMar` in that file shows no `w:top="0"` case, so passing `allowZero: false` for margins — silently replacing an author's 0" margin with the 96 px default on every .docx import — would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The proxy's `set` trap (refusing to overwrite the guarded `setPageSetup`) has no test
samples.evidence: `pageSetupGuardedStore`'s `set` trap returns `false` for `setPageSetup` with the comment "Assigning over the guard would restore the unvalidated write." In packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts I grepped `setPageSetup|Proxy|canUndo` — every assertion calls the method; none assigns to it (e.g. `store.setPageSetup = fn` should throw/no-op and the guard must survive). Deleting the `set` trap leaves all tests green while the documented bypass reopens.

samples.summary: Bound-member memoization is pinned only for stability, not for invalidation when the underlying method is replaced
samples.evidence: editor-page-setup.test.ts:352 asserts `editor.getStore().canUndo === editor.getStore().canUndo` (identity stability). The docstring also claims "a method replaced on the store (a test spy) is still picked up" — the `cached.raw === raw` check. No test replaces a method on the underlying store and re-reads it through `getStore()`, so dropping that check (caching forever) would pass.

samples.summary: `formatSourcePosition`'s hardest documented table case (a down-left rectangle whose first cell is neither endpoint) is untested
samples.evidence: The docstring says "for a down-left drag the rectangle's first cell is neither endpoint", which is the case that only the ordered rectangle can resolve. packages/docs/test/view/editor-format-painter.test.ts covers a single-row (1×2) table dragged right-to-left, where the first cell IS one of the endpoints — an implementation reading `normalized.start`'s endpoint block rather than `rect.start.rowIndex/colIndex` on a multi-row table would still pass. No multi-row cell-rectangle test exists in that file.

samples.summary: `resolvePageSetup`'s orientation coercion and `paperSize.name` fallback are untested
samples.evidence: The rewritten resolver adds `orientation === 'landscape' ? 'landscape' : 'portrait'` and `name: storedPaper.name ?? DEFAULT...name` for CRDT data. Grepping `orientation` in packages/docs/test/model/types.test.ts shows only well-formed 'portrait'/'landscape' inputs; there is no case for a garbage/undefined orientation or a missing `paperSize.name` (the `withSetup({})` case exercises the missing-object path only).
